incidents.title: Bird strike on number 2 engine, airframe inspection required
incidents.description: The crew reported a thump on the right hand side of the fuselage followed by an EGT indication change on the number 2 engine while climbing through 4,000 ft. Bird remains were recovered from the spoiler bay panel. The aircraft landed normally at Bengaluru and a leading edge nick was found on blade 1.

risk.notes: Structural integrity check pending; blade within serviceable limits.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Uncommanded engine surge during cruise climb
incidents.description: Approximately 40 minutes after take-off from Delhi, the crew observed an uncommanded thrust surge on the number 2 engine accompanied by an EGT rise of 34 °C. The crew executed the memory items, shut the engine down and continued to Bengaluru as a single-engine flight. An engine control unit chip failure is suspected on the ground.

risk.notes: Uncommanded thrust event with latent secondary damage potential.

incidents.immediateActions: ENG-2 shut down in accordance with the QRH. Flight continued single-engine to BLR with emergency services standing by. EECU removed and quarantined for bench investigation.

incidents.title: Runway excursion onto grass shoulder during landing
incidents.description: During a wet runway landing at Chennai the aircraft veered right after nose-wheel touchdown. The main gear left the paved surface and came to rest on the shoulder approximately 90 m past the design touchdown zone. No serious injuries. The investigation has identified a degraded brake temperature sensor as a likely contributor.

risk.notes: Excursion with ARFF involvement and elevated public interest exposure.

incidents.immediateActions: Aircraft recovered under ARFF actions with towbar and steering. Brake temperature sensor removed and tested. Aircraft returned to service after rectification.

incidents.title: Cabin smoke detector activation, galley fault suspected
incidents.description: The aft galley smoke detector activated at approximately 38,000 ft prompting the crew to check the related fire-handling page. No smoke was found. The galley was shut down and the flight continued to Mumbai. Post-flight inspection revealed a scorched toaster element beneath the oven.

risk.notes: Contained on board; cabin smoke remains a high-consequence event class.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Left hydraulic system low level indication in cruise
incidents.description: The crew received a low level caution for the left hydraulic system. The cross-system was configured and the flight continued to Hyderabad. Line maintenance traced the condition to a failed pressure transducer; no hydraulic leak was found.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: FMS fault, reversionary mode selected
incidents.description: A single DCDU fault indication was observed by the crew during the climb. The FMS reverted to reversionary mode and the flight was re-planned manually. The unit was removed on arrival.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Fuel quantity discrepancy between gauging and uplink
incidents.description: Pre-departure fuel reconciliation showed a 480 kg discrepancy between the gauging system and the vendor uplink figure. The load was re-verified and the flight operated with upland tanks. Uplink calibration remains under review.

risk.notes: Fuel figures are safety critical at the gate; the root cause is not yet established.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Brake wear below limit at pre-flight inspection
incidents.description: A pre-flight inspection found brake wear at 1.8 mm against a 2.5 mm limit. The defect was outside MEL limits so dispatch was held pending an engineering assessment and the aircraft was swapped.
incidents.immediateActions: Dispatch held. Aircraft substituted with VT-ANL. Brake assembly sent for dimensional inspection.

incidents.title: Cabin altitude excursion on manual pressurisation
incidents.description: The crew observed cabin altitude rising to 8,900 ft with the pressurisation system in manual mode. The standby controller was selected and the cabin was returned to normal. A control panel fault indication was noted.

risk.notes: Hypoxia risk in a single aisle cabin; classified as a serious incident.

incidents.immediateActions: Oxygen masks checked, no deployment required. Flight continued to DEL. Panel replaced on arrival.

incidents.title: Jet blast damage to GPU cable during pushback
incidents.description: A ground power unit cable was damaged by jet blast during pushback. The GPU was repositioned and the cable replaced. No aircraft damage was sustained.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Near miss: unstable approach below glide path at 500 ft
incidents.description: The aircraft was flown below the glide path on an ILS approach in IMC. A go around was initiated at approximately 220 ft when the crew recognised the deviation. Reported as a near miss and used for recurrent simulator training.

risk.notes: Approach instability in IMC is a leading contributor to controlled flight into terrain.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Tyre sidewall damage on taxiway, FOD suspected
incidents.description: During taxi the crew felt a vibration. Inspection revealed a sidewall cut on the number 2 main gear tyre. Foreign object debris was suspected from an adjacent construction area.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Engine oil consumption above trend on number 1 engine
incidents.description: Routine oil servicing records showed a step increase in consumption on the number 1 engine. The engine was removed for borescope and the oil was analysed in the laboratory.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Ramp vehicle incursion on stand, wingtip clearance marginal
incidents.description: A catering high-lift vehicle approached the stand without marshaller clearance and passed within 1.2 m of the left wingtip. The marshaller called a stop. A stand clearance briefing was re-issued to all handlers.

risk.notes: Ground incursion with a credible wingtip strike outcome.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Flight control trim run-away caution on take-off
incidents.description: A trim run-away caution was displayed shortly after rotation. The crew cut the trim motors and continued with a modified trim profile. A faulty trim switch assembly was subsequently isolated.

risk.notes: Take-off phase control event with potential loss of control authority.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Aircraft struck by lightning on the ground at Delhi
incidents.description: A ground strike was recorded on the nose radome while the aircraft was parked. The transponder and external power were unaffected and the aircraft was released after an electrical walk-around.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Crew fatigue risk assessment triggered, sector extended
incidents.description: The flight was dispatched with an extended duty period after a technical delay. A fatigue risk assessment was completed and an augmented crew was provided. Reported for trend analysis.

risk.notes: Duty time exceedance is a recognised precursor to human factors error.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: APU failure on stand, aircraft towed to gate
incidents.description: The APU failed to start after a two attempt relight on the stand. The aircraft was towed and the flight operated on ground power with a subsequent schedule delay.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Wing ice accumulation indication during approach
incidents.description: A slip indication and a brief roll oscillation were reported on approach in icing conditions. Recorded as a non-compliant practice pending review of the contamination check procedure.

risk.notes: Wing contamination; contamination check cadence under review.

incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Oxygen mask deployment, high altitude cabin alert
incidents.description: Masks deployed in the forward cabin following a high altitude cabin alert. The flight descended immediately to 10,000 ft. The pack controller was found latched in the closed position.

risk.notes: Uncommanded mask deployment; emergency descent executed.

incidents.immediateActions: Masks reset and oxygen supply verified. Flight continued to BOM. Pack controller replaced.

incidents.title: Cowl fan blade rub indication during cruise
incidents.description: Engine monitoring recorded a temporary cowl fan blade rub signature on engine 1. The flight was diverted to the nearest suitable airport. Fan case inspection found light rubbing only.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Door 2 slide deferred under MEL
incidents.description: A pre-flight check found the passenger slide indication in fault. The defect was certified under the MEL and the aircraft operated normally.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: Rudder asymmetry on landing, control cable tension
incidents.description: Post-flight inspection found asymmetric rudder pedal feel. No hydraulic leak was identified. The flight control cable tension was found outside the tolerance band.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

incidents.title: FOD ingestion indication, borescope required
incidents.description: A foreign object ingestion indication was captured on the number 1 engine during the take-off roll. The engine was borescoped and a small piece of rubber was recovered.
incidents.immediateActions: Crew returned to base under emergency or precautionary procedures. Maintenance control notified and the aircraft placed under control pending technical inspection. No further damage to the airframe was recorded.

investigations.name: Engine Failure Investigation

stageHistory.note: EECU bench test and FDM download requested.

findings: ECU firmware build 4.2.1 exhibits a known open defect in the fuel-metering trim path.
Airframe recorder data shows a 0.4 s thrust overshoot before the crew intervened.

interviews.name: Capt. V. Raghavan
interviews.summary: Described an abrupt thrust change with no control input. Response was immediate and per QRH.

interviews.name: M. Qureshi
interviews.summary: Confirmed no abnormal start or bleed configuration at the time of the event.

openQuestions: Why was build 4.2.1 fitted to a fleet with an open defect bulletin?
Has the same event occurred on other operators of this engine type?

investigations.name: Bird Strike Investigation

stageHistory.note: Blade NDT complete; remains identified as Ploceus.

findings: Leading edge nick of 3.2 mm, within the serviceable limit for the blade profile.
Strike altitude 4,000 ft corresponds to a high-density flocking period at the departure end of RWY 09R.
openQuestions: Should departure-end flock dispersal be increased for the morning departure bank?

investigations.name: Runway Excursion Investigation

stageHistory.note: QAR data, FDR download, ARFF report, ATC transcript.

findings: Right brake temperature sensor resistance drift of 18% above the acceptable band.
Anti-skid reversion was commanded 2.1 s after touchdown as designed.
Landing was conducted on a wet runway 90 m into the touchdown zone with a 10 kt tailwind component.

interviews.name: Capt. A. Bose
interviews.summary: Reported asymmetric deceleration and a right yaw tendency immediately after touchdown.

openQuestions: Why did the sensor drift pass the functional check?
Is the functional check interval appropriate for this part number?

investigations.name: FMS Reversionary Mode Investigation
findings: DCDU fault log shows a single non-recurring fault frame on channel 2.
openQuestions: Is the connector pin retention within specification?

investigations.name: Cabin Pressure Investigation

stageHistory.note: Pack controller bench test; control panel harness.

findings: Outflow valve actuator exhibited intermittent position feedback loss.
Cabin altitude reached 8,900 ft; oxygen supply remained available throughout.

interviews.name: F/O S. Iyer
interviews.summary: Stated the standby controller engaged without an intervening crew selection.

openQuestions: Does the pack controller self-test cover the outflow valve feedback path?

investigations.name: Oil Consumption Trend Investigation
findings: Laboratory analysis shows metallic content within limits; no wear debris signature yet.
openQuestions: Is the servicing interval adequate given the observed step change?

investigations.name: APU Start Failure Investigation
findings: Bleed air supply pressure marginal at the start valve during the second attempt.

investigations.name: Mask Deployment Investigation
findings: Pack controller latch mechanism remained engaged from a previous maintenance action.
openQuestions: Was the maintenance action correctly recorded against the pack controller?

investigations.name: Rudder Feel Discrepancy Investigation
findings: Right cable tension measured 118 N against a tolerance of 95–105 N.

rcas.title: Uncommanded thrust surge — engine control unit

factors.label: ECU firmware defect
factors.detail: Firmware build 4.2.1 contains an open defect in the fuel-metering trim path, permitting an uncommanded thrust correction.

factors.label: Bulletin not actioned
factors.detail: Service bulletin SB-ENG-441 was issued 6 weeks before the event and had not been embodied across the fleet.

factors.label: Line maintenance finding
factors.detail: The removed ECU displayed a previous "watch item" entry that was closed without technical justification.

factors.label: Crew recognition time
factors.detail: 0.4 s elapsed between the thrust change and the first crew input. Recognition and action were within limits.

factors.label: No contributing factor
factors.detail: Ambient conditions were outside the published envelope for the defect to manifest as observed.

identifiedRootCauses: Un-embodied service bulletin SB-ENG-441 leaving the known firmware defect in service.
Weak governance over deferred watch items in the line maintenance record.
recommendations: Embody SB-ENG-441 across all affected ECUs within 14 days.
Re-review every open watch item for the type with the Chief Engineer.
Introduce a mandatory firmware build verification at each heavy check.

fiveWhys.rootCause: The fleet was operating with a known un-embodied engine control unit firmware defect, and the assurance process for service bulletins and deferred watch items was insufficient to prevent it entering service.

whys.question: Why did the engine fail?
whys.answer: The engine control unit issued an uncommanded fuel-metering trim correction producing a 12% thrust overshoot.

whys.question: Why did the component fail?
whys.answer: The ECU was running firmware build 4.2.1 which contains an uncorrected defect in the metering trim path.

whys.question: Why was the defect not detected?
whys.answer: Build 4.2.1 passed the bench functional test because the test vector does not exercise the metering trim path.

whys.question: Why was the inspection insufficient?
whys.answer: The functional test was not updated after the software standard changed, and no regression vector was added.

whys.question: Why was the inspection procedure inadequate?
whys.answer: Engineering change control did not require regression test updates when a software build was superseded on an installed unit.

rcas.title: Bird strike — departure end flocking exposure

factors.label: Flocking period
factors.detail: The strike occurred during a documented morning flocking period at the departure end of RWY 09R.

factors.label: Dispersal timing
factors.detail: Wildlife dispersal runs were scheduled 40 minutes before the first departure, allowing reaccumulation.

factors.label: Dispersal contract oversight
factors.detail: Contractor dispersal performance is not audited against flight departure density.

factors.label: Structural tolerance
factors.detail: Leading edge damage of 3.2 mm remained within the serviceable limit for the blade profile.

identifiedRootCauses: Wildlife dispersal timing does not align with the morning departure bank density.
recommendations: Re-baseline dispersal frequency to a maximum 20 minute interval during the morning bank.
Add departure density to the wildlife control KPI set.

fiveWhys.problem: Bird strike on the number 2 engine during the initial climb.
fiveWhys.rootCause: Wildlife dispersal cadence was set against hourly counts rather than against departure density, allowing bird activity to rebuild within the climb corridor.

whys.question: Why did the bird strike occur?
whys.answer: A flock was present in the departure corridor during the initial climb segment.

whys.question: Why was a flock present in the departure corridor?
whys.answer: Dispersal had last been performed 41 minutes before departure.

whys.question: Why had 41 minutes elapsed?
whys.answer: The dispersal interval is fixed at 40 minutes during peak hours.

whys.question: Why is the interval fixed?
whys.answer: The interval was set from hourly bird count data, not from departure density.

whys.question: Why has the interval not been risk based?
whys.answer: Departure density is not currently captured in the wildlife hazard assessment model.

rcas.title: Runway excursion — brake temperature sensing chain

factors.label: Sensor resistance drift
factors.detail: Right brake temperature sensor resistance drifted 18% above the acceptable band, biasing the anti-skid control module.

factors.label: Functional check scope
factors.detail: The functional check verified indication only and did not compare raw sensor resistance against the reference curve.

factors.label: Interval not risk based
factors.detail: The check interval for this part number was inherited from a legacy platform and never re-assessed.

factors.label: Landing technique
factors.detail: Touchdown was 90 m into the zone with a 10 kt tailwind component, within limits but not conservative.

factors.label: Wet runway
factors.detail: Standing water in the touchdown zone reduced available friction below the planned figure.

identifiedRootCauses: Brake temperature sensor drift was outside the detectable capability of the functional check as written.
The check interval for the part number has not been reassessed since introduction.
recommendations: Amend the functional check to include a raw resistance comparison against the reference curve.
Re-assess the check interval for the part number on a 12 month cycle.
Issue a fleet advisory and brief all crews on conservative wet runway touchdown techniques.

fiveWhys.problem: Aircraft departed the runway surface during a wet runway landing.
fiveWhys.rootCause: A brake temperature sensor resistance drift degraded the anti-skid control module input, and neither the functional check as written nor its interval was capable of detecting the condition before it affected a wet runway landing.

whys.question: Why did the aircraft leave the runway surface?
whys.answer: Right wheel braking was materially less effective than left, producing a yaw that the crew could not fully control.

whys.question: Why was right braking less effective?
whys.answer: The anti-skid control module was supplied a biased right brake temperature signal and modulated the right brake release incorrectly.

whys.question: Why was the sensor signal biased?
whys.answer: The sensor resistance had drifted 18% above the acceptable band with no warning indication in the cockpit.

whys.question: Why was the drift not detected before flight?
whys.answer: The functional check validated the cockpit indication chain only, never the raw sensor resistance against the reference curve.

whys.question: Why has the check not detected this in the fleet?
whys.answer: The check was inherited unchanged from a legacy platform and has never been risk assessed for this part number.

rcas.title: Hydraulic low level indication — transducer integrity

factors.label: Transducer failure
factors.detail: The left hydraulic low level pressure transducer failed open, producing a spurious low level caution.

factors.label: Leak check omission
factors.detail: The troubleshooting procedure did not include a circuit capacitance check before sensor replacement.

identifiedRootCauses: A circuit capacitance check is missing from the troubleshooting procedure.
recommendations: Insert a capacitance check at step 4 of the low level caution troubleshooting card.
Sweep the transducer part number for similar open circuit failures across the fleet.

rcas.title: Fuel gauging discrepancy — uplink calibration

factors.label: Uplink calibration
factors.detail: The vendor fuel upland system uses a fixed density factor that does not match the actual fuel loaded.

factors.label: Reconciliation practice
factors.detail: Reconciliation thresholds are advisory and were overridden twice in the preceding quarter.

factors.label: No escalation rule
factors.detail: No rule escalates a repeated discrepancy at the same station to the fuel team.

identifiedRootCauses: Uplink density factor is not station specific.
recommendations: Request a station specific density calibration from the vendor.
Introduce a mandatory escalation after two reconciliations within seven days.

rcas.title: Cabin altitude excursion — outflow valve feedback

factors.label: Outflow valve feedback
factors.detail: The outflow valve actuator intermittently lost position feedback, allowing the pack to command a cabin climb.

factors.label: Self test coverage
factors.detail: The pack self test does not exercise the outflow valve feedback path.

factors.label: Monitoring
factors.detail: The crew detected the excursion on the standby instrument at 7,200 ft cabin altitude.

identifiedRootCauses: Outflow valve feedback is not covered by the pack self test.
recommendations: Extend the pack self test to include a valve feedback plausibility check.
Evaluate the pack controller with the vendor for a latch monitoring improvement.

fiveWhys.problem: Cabin altitude rose to 8,900 ft in manual pressurisation mode.
fiveWhys.rootCause: The outflow valve feedback path is not monitored by the pack self test, so an intermittent feedback loss was not detected before it produced a cabin altitude excursion.

whys.question: Why did the cabin altitude rise?
whys.answer: The pack continued to command outflow for a closed valve because it had lost position feedback.

whys.question: Why was position feedback lost?
whys.answer: The actuator position transducer coupling intermittently slipped under vibration.

whys.question: Why was the loss not detected?
whys.answer: The pack self test does not plausibility check the valve feedback against commanded position.

whys.question: Why is the check absent?
whys.answer: The self test was designed against the original actuator which had a captive feedback link.

whys.question: Why was the actuator change not covered?
whys.answer: Modification control does not require a review of dependent system self test coverage.

rcas.title: Approach instability in IMC

factors.label: Glide path monitoring
factors.detail: The deviation was not called until 500 ft, below the company monitoring call height.

factors.label: Call height ambiguity
factors.detail: The IMC call height table does not define a lower monitoring call for a low visibility approach.

factors.label: Low visibility
factors.detail: Visibility 400 m in rain with a broken ceiling reduced the available visual references.

identifiedRootCauses: The monitoring call height table has no entry for low visibility ILS approaches.
recommendations: Add a 1,000 ft monitoring call for approaches below 500 m visibility.
Revise the approach briefing template to include the monitoring call height explicitly.

rcas.title: Ground vehicle incursion — stand clearance control

factors.label: Stand clearance
factors.detail: The handler proceeded without an engine running clearance from the marshaller.

factors.label: Handler training records
factors.detail: Two of four handlers on the stand had records pending for the new high-lift vehicle type.

factors.label: Task saturation
factors.detail: The handler was managing a simultaneous pushback and cabin service request.

identifiedRootCauses: Handler training records were incomplete for the high-lift vehicle type.
recommendations: Suspend high-lift operations at the stand until all handler records are current.
Introduce a positive clearance readback requirement for all stand movements.

rcas.title: Trim run-away — switch assembly

factors.label: Switch assembly
factors.detail: A trim switch assembly showed internal pitting consistent with a failed seal allowing moisture ingress.

factors.label: Moisture detection absent
factors.detail: No cockpit indication exists for moisture in the trim switch bay.

identifiedRootCauses: No environmental sealing was applied to the trim switch assembly during manufacture.
recommendations: Replace the affected switch assemblies across the fleet.
Raise a manufacturer technical query on sealing.

rcas.title: Wing contamination on approach

factors.label: Contamination check
factors.detail: The contamination check did not cover the upper wing surface above the engine pylon.

factors.label: Check discipline
factors.detail: The check was performed from the ground with limited access to the upper surface.

identifiedRootCauses: The contamination check has no access provision for the upper wing surface.
recommendations: Provide a documented access method for upper surface checks.

rcas.title: FOD ingestion — airfield construction interface

factors.label: Construction interface
factors.detail: Runway reconstruction works were adjacent to the active taxiway with no joint FOD inspection.

factors.label: FOD inspection cadence
factors.detail: FOD walks are performed on a fixed hourly schedule rather than on a trigger basis.

identifiedRootCauses: No joint FOD inspection protocol exists with the construction contractor.
recommendations: Establish a joint FOD inspection protocol with the contractor.
Move to trigger based FOD walks during construction periods.

compliance.title: Occurrence reporting within prescribed timelines
compliance.description: All reportable occurrences are entered into the SMS within 24 hours with the correct occurrence category and immediate actions recorded.

compliance.title: Voluntary reporting system availability and promotion
compliance.description: The voluntary reporting channel is published, confidential and actively promoted across operational areas.
compliance.evidence: Voluntary reports up 18% year on year

compliance.title: Internal investigation of reportable occurrences
compliance.description: Each reportable occurrence is subject to a documented internal investigation with a defined stage sequence and named investigator.
compliance.evidence: 2 investigations passed their target date in the last quarter

compliance.title: Evidence handling and chain of custody
compliance.description: Physical and digital evidence is registered, hash verified and retained for the mandated retention period.
compliance.evidence: Audit of 60 evidence items, 58 hash verified

compliance.title: Corrective and preventive action closure process
compliance.description: Actions are raised against identified findings, tracked to a named owner, and closed only after an effectiveness check.
compliance.evidence: 3 overdue actions outstanding beyond the SLA

compliance.title: Effectiveness verification of completed actions
compliance.description: Completed actions are subject to a documented effectiveness check, sampled independently of the action owner.
compliance.evidence: Verification register under sample by the audit team

compliance.title: Safety record keeping and retention
compliance.description: Safety records are complete, legible, retrievable and retained for the period specified by the applicable rules.
compliance.evidence: No retention exceptions raised in the last audit

compliance.title: Controlled document distribution and revision control
compliance.description: Procedures are issued at the correct revision and superseded copies are withdrawn from operational areas.
compliance.evidence: 14 superseded copies found during the last line audit

compliance.title: Internal audit programme coverage
compliance.description: The internal audit programme covers all SMS elements at the defined frequency with findings tracked to closure.
compliance.evidence: 2 of 11 planned audits closed, 5 findings open

compliance.title: Continuous monitoring and trending of safety performance
compliance.description: Safety performance indicators are defined, trended and reported to management at the agreed cadence.
compliance.evidence: Monthly safety review pack issued on schedule

compliance.title: Safety management system review and amendment
compliance.description: The SMS is reviewed on a scheduled basis and amendments are made when operational experience indicates a change is required.
compliance.evidence: Annual review in progress, two amendments drafted

compliance.title: Occurrence investigation and reporting obligations
compliance.description: Investigations satisfy the state occurrence investigation requirements including independence and reporting timelines.
compliance.evidence: 1 investigation exceeded the regulatory reporting window

compliance.title: Lessons learned dissemination across operational areas
compliance.description: Investigation findings and lessons learned are disseminated to all affected operational areas in a timely manner.
compliance.evidence: Findings distributed to 6 bases within 5 working days

compliance.title: Personnel training on safety procedures
compliance.description: All personnel in safety critical roles are trained and assessed on the applicable SMS procedures and their updates.
compliance.evidence: 11 training records outstanding across ground handling
